prompt: Write the client side of a one-line conversation: connect to 127.0.0.1 on a given port, send a line, and return the single line the server sends back. Complete askServer, then run the tests.
explanation: A Socket gives you two streams -- getOutputStream() to send and getInputStream() to receive -- and wrapping them in a BufferedWriter and BufferedReader lets you work in lines of text instead of raw bytes. Buffered output sits in memory until you flush it, so a missing flush() is the classic cause of a client that hangs waiting for a reply it never asked for. try-with-resources closes the socket for you even if reading throws, and readLine() hands back the reply without its trailing newline.
hints: new Socket("127.0.0.1", port) connects; put it in a try-with-resources so the socket always closes.
Wrap socket.getOutputStream() in an OutputStreamWriter and a BufferedWriter, write the message and a "\n", then call flush().
Wrap socket.getInputStream() in an InputStreamReader and a BufferedReader and return readLine() -- it strips the newline for you.
